drawn.title: Associate
drawn.body: <div class="content-intro"><p>MIO Partners Inc. (MIO) is a global, world-class investment and advisory institution with a decades-long track record of performance for our clients through multiple market cycles. Our team of approximately 250 people provides asset management and advisory services to current and former McKinsey employees. We manage more than $20 billion in assets across public and private markets. We are headquartered in New York City, with offices in Atlanta, Georgia; &nbsp;West Palm Beach, Florida; Germany; Hong Kong; Singapore; Spain; and the UK.</p> <p>We provide objective advice on long-term wealth building and create distinctive investment products that deliver value relative to market-based benchmarks. We operate two core lines of business: (i) our advisory team provides advice, wealth planning, and retirement services to approximately 2500 individual clients, and (ii) our investments business consists of alpha-seeking alternative investment strategies across public and private markets.&nbsp;</p> <p>A defining characteristic of our business is our perfect alignment with our clients. Our extraordinary mandate as a boutique investment and advisory firm, grounded in a core set of principles, enables us to create unique products and services while keeping our clients’ interests front and center.&nbsp;</p> <p>Much of our success can be attributed to our insatiable intellectual curiosity. We seek to hire individuals who are passionate about our mission and values, and who always strive toward excellence. We care about fostering a culture of continual improvement, as individuals and as an organization, and are excited to work with individuals who have a similar growth mindset. We are proud to have a culture that promotes the highest ethical standards and investor-focused values, alongside a commitment to diversity and inclusivity and a highly collaborative work environment.</p> <p>MIO (and related entities) is an independent, indirect, and wholly owned subsidiary of McKinsey &amp; Company.&nbsp;</p></div><p><strong><em>Position</em></strong></p> <p>As a member of MIO’s investment team, the Associate role is ideal for those pursuing a long-term career in investment management with a focus on research and market analysis. The position offers the opportunity to develop deep content expertise, support portfolio strategy, and contribute to proprietary insights used across the firm. This is a long-term, early-career opportunity (3–5-year commitment preferred). It is not suited for candidates seeking short-term roles or those uninterested in data-driven analysis of financial markets.</p> <p><strong><em>Primary responsibilities&nbsp;</em></strong></p> <p>The Associate will be responsible for supporting tasks related to creating new</p> <p>&nbsp;research and maintaining existing research. Their principal duties will include:</p> <ul> <li>Understanding the research agenda and starting to develop content-area expertise</li> <li>Working with a Portfolio Manager and/or Associate Portfolio Manager to apply both qualitative and quantitative approaches to test investment hypotheses</li> <li>Developing intuition for the behavior of key market actors and how they can drive pricing inefficiencies</li> <li>Finding and selecting raw data inputs, producing research outputs (for example, an ongoing dashboard monitoring a relationship or a one-time white paper determining the nature of a relationship), and documenting the research methodology</li> <li>Ownership over existing body of research, thoroughly understanding the content, making substantial content improvements (i.e., insights, usability, visual quality), managing and improving the processes for keeping our research output updated (e.g., automating and systematizing the production of ongoing research). Wherever possible, integrating research so that insights from multiple research streams can be combined to produce new insights.</li> <li>Actively assist in systematizing MIO’s quantitative research, including standardizing research production and developing/managing a portion of MIO’s quantitative research database (including metadata maintenance and streamlining), at times working closely with the Investment IT team. Optimizing macroeconomic and financial data sourcing across the organization.</li> <li>Potentially supporting Portfolio Managers and/or Associate Portfolio Managers in implementing and monitoring trades to provide perspective on and validation of their strategies and hypotheses</li> </ul> <p><strong><em>Desired background</em></strong></p> <p>The most important qualities for an Investment Associate are strong analytical thinking, intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, and the ability to translate complex information into practical investment insights. A commitment to producing high-quality work, openness to new ideas, and alignment with a values-oriented rather than solely profit-driven environment, where the best interests of our investors come before personal objectives, are also critical to success in the role.</p> <p>The Associate will need to be comfortable manipulating large datasets drawing intuitive conclusions, and then communicating findings clearly and visually to both technical and non-technical audiences.&nbsp;The ability to connect research findings to market behavior and practical investment decisions is more important than technical or theoretical sophistication alone.</p> <p>Prior knowledge and experience with financial markets and/or macroeconomic concepts, terminology, and data would be helpful in enabling the candidate to quickly learn our existing research and be more immediately productive in creating new research.</p> <p>Ideal qualifications include:</p> <ul> <li>0-2.5 years of professional work experience strongly preferred, not required</li> <li>Undergraduate degree with a record of outstanding academic achievement (required)</li> <li>Coursework in finance, business, and economics is highly desirable (and may be required for certain roles)</li> <li>High proficiency in Excel is required. Familiarity with Bloomberg and experience creating clear charts or dashboards are helpful. Experience using Python, coding agents and other AI tools to accelerate research, analysis, and coding is a plus, but not required&nbsp;</li> <li>Working knowledge of Bloomberg; knowledge of other industry-standard macroeconomic and financial market data sources (e.g., IHS Global Insights, Markit, Haver, Thomson Reuters DataStream, S&amp;P Capital IQ, Moody’s Economy.com)</li> </ul> <p>Key Competencies &amp; Attributes:</p> <ul> <li>Attention to detail; ability to prioritize accuracy over false precision</li> <li>Strong, naturally curious problem-solver (e.g., issue identification, structuring)</li> <li>Comfort with both qualitative and quantitative methodologies to approach (and simplify) complex questions</li> <li>Strong mathematical, analytical, and quantitative skills</li> <li>Excellent communication skills: ability to communicate complex concepts in simple terms and to link quantitative insight with business logic and intuition</li> <li>Team player who places the best interests of the firm above personal objectives</li> <li>Integrity; strong personal values; work ethic; maturity</li> <li>Desire to work in a values-oriented environment focused on maximizing returns for our investors</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>&nbsp;</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>Certain US states require MIO Partners, Inc. to include a reasonable estimate of the salary range for this role.&nbsp;Actual salaries may vary and may be above or below the range based on various factors, including, but not limited to an individual’s assigned office location, experience, and expertise.&nbsp;Certain roles are also eligible for bonuses, subject to MIO’s discretion and based on factors such as individual and/or organizational performance.&nbsp;Additionally, MIO offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental and vision coverage, telemedicine services, life, accident and disability insurance, parental leave and family planning benefits, caregiving resources, a generous retirement program, financial guidance, and paid time off.</em></p></div><div class="title">Base salary range</div><div class="pay-range"><span>$130,000</span><span class="divider">&mdash;</span><span>$130,000 USD</span></div></div></div><div class="content-conclusion"><p style="text-align: left;"><em><span data-contrast="auto">MIO Partners, Inc. drawn.title: Private Funds Advisory - Distribution Associate
drawn.body:
Job Description:

At Piper Sandler, we connect capital with opportunity to build a better future.

We believe diverse teams with unique backgrounds, skills and experiences yield more innovative solutions. Our mission is to recruit, develop, retain and engage a high-performing team. Our business enables bright, committed people working in partnership within an environment that allows each person to achieve at a high level. We commit to encouraging and valuing inclusivity because every partner brings unique perspectives that help us better serve our clients.

Piper Sandler’s Private Capital Advisory group (“PCA”) provides comprehensive, tailored solutions throughout an alternative investment manager’s lifecycle. PCA operates across three core business lines: Private Funds, Secondary Capital Advisory, and Capital Solutions.

We are currently looking for a Private Funds Distribution Associate to join the Private Funds Group (“PFG”) in Dallas.

The associate will support the placement of private-market investment funds with investors in the Midwest, Southand West Coast helping senior team members develop investor relationships and execute fundraising mandates. The associate will support the distribution of multiple fundraising mandates simultaneously, helping ensure effective communication among fund managers, investors, and internal teams. This client-facing role requires strong interpersonal and organizational skills, an interest in the alternative investment industry, and the ability to manage multiple workstreams in a fast-paced environment. The role offers exposure to investor coverage, fundraising strategy, and collaboration across PCA’s core business lines.

Key deal execution tasks include:

· Support senior team members in maintaining and developing relationships with LPs, consultants, and other institutional and high-net-worth investors in the Midwest, South and West Coast Regions
· Assist with the execution of fundraising mandates, including investor targeting, outreach, meeting preparation, follow-up, and process tracking
· Develop working knowledge of GP clients, fund products, investment strategies, and target investor profiles; help communicate each client’s value proposition to prospective investors
· Prepare and maintain investor materials, meeting notes, coverage plans, and CRM records, including timely updates to CRM
· Coordinate investor meetings, roadshows, due diligence sessions, and follow-up processes.
· Monitor investor allocation trends, market activity, competitors, and relevant private-markets developments; share insights with the team
· Work collaboratively with project management and colleagues across PCA to support a coordinated client and investor experience
· Contribute to PFG’s broader growth by identifying opportunities to deepen investor coverage and improve fundraising execution
· Ad hoc projects and other work as assigned

Qualifications include:

• 3–5 years of relevant experience in private-fund fundraising, placement agency, institutional sales or investor coverage, private-markets investor relations, alternatives distribution, or investment banking
• Experience supporting capital-raising, investor-coverage, or other client-facing processes preferred
• Strong communication and relationship-management skills, with the ability to engage professionally with investors, clients, and colleagues
• Strong analytical skills and the ability to understand investment strategies and financial materials
• Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple fundraising workstreams and deadlines
• Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint required; experience with DealCloud or another CRM platform preferred
• Bachelor’s degree required; a degree in finance, economics, accounting, or a related field preferred
• FINRA SIE, 7, 63 licenses or the ability to obtain them within the applicable timeframe

As a leading investment bank, we enable growth and success for our clients through deep sector expertise, candid advice and a differentiated, highly productive culture.

Our investment banking clients have access to unparalleled guidance through our deep product and sector expertise and ready access to global capital. We take pride in providing our clients with thoughtful advice and diligent execution, no matter the economic environment. Our investment banking group partners with corporate clients and financial sponsors to provide advisory and financing services related to mergers and acquisitions, equity and debt capital markets, private placements, restructuring and corporate & venture services. We offer in-depth knowledge and industry relationships in our core sectors of chemicals, consumer, diversified industrials & services, energy & power, financial services, healthcare and technology. Learn more about our investment banking team here .

Piper Sandler values a strong culture dedicated to the emotional and physical well-being of our employees. Learn more about our commitment to our employee’s health and well-being. Learn more about our benefits program and how we are here for our employees and their families today, tomorrow and beyond.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, marital status, status as a protected veteran or status with regard to public assistance.

The anticipated starting salary for Dallas-based individuals expressing interest in this position ranges from $175,000 - $225,000 per year. Placement within this range is dependent upon level of experience. This position is eligible for annual incentive compensation which will be a part of the total compensation. Total compensation for this position will be competitive with the market.

Job Summary
Be a problem solver, trusted advisor, and partner to the people and businesses in our KeyBank communities. Personal Bankers engage clients in deeper conversations to uncover needs and provide guidance and solutions to assist in client's financial wellness both in person and through proactive calling efforts. As part of the branch team, the Personal Banker will work toward attracting new clients to Key and work with existing clients to develop and expand relationships based on their unique financial goals, leading to client confidence in their finances. The Personal Banker is a client first, sales-driven, self-motivated, and competitive individual. Strong and effective teamwork, paired with communication polish and confidence, are critical for this role. At KeyBank, we believe it's our opportunity and our privilege to help our clients move forward in their financial journey. We take pride in serving our clients and making them feel that no bank will fight harder for them.

Essential Functions
• Embodies a strong client experience culture, being present with every client and teammate and realizing the impact we can have on their day, personally, professionally, and financially.
• Listen for clues for financial wellness opportunities during in-person and over the phone client conversations and provide effective and customized financial wellness recommendations to clients.
• Consistently attains individual activity, behavior, and outcome goals and expectations.

• Bachelor's Degree (preferred)

KeyBank provides the tools and training, but we need relationship builders with a curious nature who are great at sparking conversations. (required)

Skills
• Is knowledgeable about the client’s accounts and business with the bank and uses sound judgment with clients and transactions.

• Strong work ethic and high level of integrity.
• Excellent time management skills.
• Building and nurturing relationships with clients including identifying potential clients, engaging with them to understand their needs, and developing strategies to convert them into long-term clients. It also includes deepening relationships with existing clients by offering additional products and services that meet their evolving needs.
• Being attentive to client needs, resolving issues promptly, and ensuring a positive banking experience. Excellent client service helps build trust and encourages clients to continue banking with KeyBank.
• Ability to evaluate financial information to understand clients' financial health, identify investment opportunities, and recommend strategies.
• Understanding and managing risks associated with banking operations and client transactions.
• Strong verbal and non-verbal communication skills to understand clients' needs and recommend appropriate banking products and services.
• Accurate and efficient handling of cash transactions.

Core Competencies
• All KeyBank employees are expected to demonstrate Key’s Values and abide by Key’s Code of Conduct.

Job Summary
Be a problem solver, trusted advisor, and partner to the people and businesses in our KeyBank communities. The Private Client Banker (PCB) is part of the Key Private Client Program and will focus on the entire client relationship with a plan-based approach to financial advice. As a PCB, you will deliver and refer appropriate financial solutions to KeyBank's client base with up to $2M in investable assets. The PCB helps new and existing clients achieve confidence in their financial wellness by assessing their financial needs, gathering and documenting client data, and offering appropriate products and services. PCBs identify products and services to meet client needs and refer to appropriate sales professionals in Retail, Key Investment Services, Private Bank, Mortgage or Business Banking. At KeyBank, we believe it's our opportunity and our privilege to help our clients move forward in their financial journey. We take pride in serving our clients and making them feel that no bank will fight harder for them.

Essential Functions
• Embodies a strong client experience culture, being present with every client and teammate and realizing the impact we can have on their day, personally, professionally, and financially.
• Listen for clues for financial wellness opportunities during client conversations and provide effective and customized financial wellness recommendations to clients; Delivers on client solutions through referring of investment and insurance products.
• Consistently attains individual activity, behavior, and outcome goals and expectations.
• Builds a client referral pipeline via identification and development of internal and external centers of influence; Employs a disciplined approach to prospecting; documents calling efforts.
• Develops and maintains an in-depth knowledge of private client products and services, as well as knowledge of competitive products and services to ensure meaningful in-depth financial wellness conversations with clients.
• Opening personal and business accounts (consumer checking, small business, various deposit products, home equity, unsecured lending, certificates of deposit, etc.).
• Developing strong partnerships with branch teammates and line of business partners through in-person meetings– focusing on client acquisition and deepening the relationship of current clients; effectively managing internal and external centers of influence.
• Ensuring compliance with operational, risk, security and audit procedures and policies including appropriate documentation of client interactions.
• Support of branch operations including assisting with client transactions on the Teller line as needed.
• Participate in and occasionally facilitate in-person morning huddles and end of day debriefs.
• Work on Saturdays as directed by management.
• Performs other duties as assigned; duties, responsibilities and/or activities may change or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice
• Complies with all KeyBank policies and procedures, including without limitation, acting professionally at all times, conducting business ethically, avoiding conflicts of interest, and acting in the best interests of Key’s clients and Key.

Education
• High School Diploma , GED, or equivalent experience (required) or
• Bachelor's Degree (preferred)

• OR equivalent experience (required)

Work Experience
• Experience in developing current and new customer relationships, achieving sales goals and building referral sources in insurance and investment products. (required)
• Foundational knowledge of sales and service techniques with clients, including tele-consulting, outside calling, prospecting and networking. (required)
• Comfortable interacting with small business clients, overcoming objection, and asking fact-finding questions with the goal of being helpful. (preferred)
• Interpersonal interaction skills and an ability to build rapport in matter of minutes is vital. (required)
• Demonstrated experience with influencing business partners and leveraging centers of influence, as this role will require significant influence of partners such as Key Investment Services, Mortgage and Business Banking sales professionals. (required)
• Working knowledge of PCs (MS Windows and Office Products including Word, Excel, etc.). (required)
• Working knowledge of digital technology (mobile, apps, web-based browsing) and ability to educate clients on digital platforms and capabilities within Key (required)

Licenses and Certifications

• FINRA License S63 (required)
• FINRA Security Industry Essentials (SIE) (required)

Skills
• Is knowledgeable about the client’s accounts and business with the bank and uses sound judgment with clients and transactions.
• Demonstrated ability to attain sales and referral goals through preset appointments and quality conversations leading to recommendations that support clients’ financial wellness goals, leveraging system generated lead lists, walk-ins, and professional contacts.
• Strong work ethic and high level of integrity.
• Excellent time management skills.
• Providing clients with expert advice on managing their finances, including investment strategies, retirement planning, and tax optimization. This role requires assessing clients' financial situations and offering tailored advice to help them achieve their financial goals.
• Building and nurturing relationships with clients to understand their needs and provide solutions that enhance their financial well-being. This involves identifying potential clients, developing trust, and maintaining long-term relationships.
• Evaluating the overall health of a client's financial situation, including their ability to manage day-to-day finances, save for the future, and protect against financial risks. As a Private Client Banker, you will help clients achieve financial wellness through effective financial planning and advice.
• Actively identifying and developing new client relationships through prospecting and networking.
• Developing and maintaining strong relationships with high-net-worth clients, providing personalized service to meet their financial needs.
• Staying updated with market trends and analyzing market conditions to provide informed financial advice.

Core Competencies
• All KeyBank employees are expected to demonstrate Key’s Values and abide by Key’s Code of Conduct.

Physical Demands

Driving Requirements

This position is eligible to earn a base hourly rate in the range of $25.00 - $38.46 per hour. Placement within the pay range may differ based upon various factors, including but not limited to skills, experience and geographic location. Compensation for this role also includes incentive compensation which may include production, commission, and/or discretionary incentives.

drawn.title: Investment Associate
drawn.body:
ABOUT FREC

Frec is building the modern investment platform for high-net-worth investors. We combine self-directed investing with continuously managed strategies in a single brokerage account, bringing capabilities traditionally delivered through wealth managers directly to our customers.

We see AI as a way to make sophisticated investing more personal and intuitive. The investment infrastructure we’ve already built gives us a foundation to help customers make better decisions without giving up control of their financial lives.

Customers have entrusted us with $1.5 billion in assets, up 4x in the last year. We’re backed by Greylock and have reached this scale with a small team. The people who join now will help build the primary investment platform for a new generation of investors.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Portfolio Manager to oversee thousands of customer portfolios and help build an AI experience that gives every Frec customer access to a personal portfolio manager.

You’ll help ensure our portfolios are behaving as intended, understand what’s driving their performance, and investigate when something needs attention. You’ll work closely with our investment team and engineers to improve how we manage portfolios at scale.

The opportunity goes beyond overseeing portfolios. You’ll help turn your investment expertise into a product that helps customers understand their investments and make better decisions. That means shaping how AI analyzes a customer’s portfolio and explains the tradeoffs, with licensed human oversight where judgment matters most.

This is a highly technical, hands-on role for someone who knows systematic long/short equities deeply and wants to build. You should be as comfortable investigating a portfolio issue as you are collaborating with engineers to design scalable portfolio systems.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Manage portfolios at scale: Oversee thousands of customized equity accounts. Monitor performance against benchmarks, review risk exposures, and define automated checks for tracking error, cash balances, and factor exposures.

- Enhance strategies. Bring insights from live portfolios to researchers. Help refine portfolio construction, risk monitoring, risk and performance attribution, and support the testing and rollout of new investment capabilities. Help design alerts to surface unexpected behavior, focusing human attention where judgment matters most.

- Maintain tax-awareness & compliance: Consider tax-awareness throughout portfolio implementation, including awareness of US tax regulations relevant to both long only and long/short equity investing. Ensure compliance with all internal and external rules and regulations.

- Build our AI experience: Partner with product and engineering to translate your quantitative expertise into automated portfolio analysis, personalized guidance, and rigorous real-world test cases for AI outputs.

- Set a high bar for investment accuracy. Develop real-world test cases and evaluate AI-generated analysis and recommendations. Identify missing context or flawed assumptions. Work with compliance to establish appropriate boundaries and determine when a licensed professional needs to review a decision.

- Work directly with customers. Explain portfolio performance and help customers evaluate complex investment decisions, including concentrated-stock transitions and the tradeoff between tax efficiency and tracking risk. Turn recurring questions into capabilities we can build into the product.

WHAT YOU BRING

- Proven PM Experience: 5+ years of quantitative equity portfolio management with direct responsibility for decisions and outcomes—not only research or client coverage, strongly preferring experience with long/short strategies. Quantitative equity research experience is a significant plus.

- Deep expertise in equities portfolio management: You understand how market and factor exposures drive returns, how to measure risk, and how implementation choices affect performance. You’re comfortable with portfolio optimization, performance attribution, margin requirements, and the economics of financing and short borrowing. You possess solid economic intuition and good commercial instinct.

- Technical proficiency: An undergraduate or graduate degree in a STEM field, plus robust programming experience (Python, SQL) for analyzing portfolio data and collaborating with engineers.

- Exceptional execution & collaboration: You have exceptional attention to detail, are careful/thorough, well-organized, and possess effective time management skills. You thrive in a team-oriented, collaborative environment and bring a great attitude to work.

- A builder’s mindset: You experiment with AI tools and think critically about their outputs. You can translate investment reasoning into clear product requirements and recognize when an answer sounds convincing but is incomplete or wrong.

- Clear, credible communication. You can earn the trust of sophisticated investors and explain a difficult portfolio decision without hiding behind jargon. You’re comfortable discussing uncertainty and helping customers understand their options.

- Sound judgment and ownership. You notice when something doesn’t look right and follow through until you understand it. You know when to act independently and when to bring in another expert.

- An understanding of tax-aware investing is a plus. You understand tax-loss harvesting and wash-sale constraints, including the challenges of transitioning appreciated portfolios. You can evaluate tax benefits alongside investment risk and costs rather than treating harvested losses as the only measure of success.

A CFA designation is preferred, but not required. You should hold, or be willing to obtain, the registrations needed for your responsibilities.

WHAT WE OFFER:

- Competitive salary and equity grants

- Fully paid health, vision and dental insurances

- 401k

- Monthly allowance to help with maintaining a healthy body and mind (fitness & mental health components)

- Flexible (Unlimited) paid time off

- Visa sponsorship & immigration support

- Daily in-office lunch and dinner

- Office in San Francisco/New York for in-person collaboration (close to public transit options)

CONTACT:

If all of the above resonates with you, reach out to us at careers@frec.com and join us for the ride!

drawn.title: IB Analyst - Real Estate
drawn.body: IB Analyst - Real Estate Location US-MO-Saint Louis ID 2026-9923 Category Institutional Position Type Regular | Full Time Work Type Onsite Why Stifel Stifel strives for a culture that puts its clients and associates first: a culture where everyone belongs, everyone is welcome, and everyone contributes to the success of our clients, their careers, and the firm as a whole. Let’s talk about how you can find your place here at Stifel, where success meets success . What You'll Be Doing Under general supervision, the Investment Banking Analyst supports Stifel’s Real Estate Investment Banking Group, which provides advisory and capital-raising services to Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and Real Estate Operating Companies (REOCs). The Analyst is responsible for conducting industry and property-sector research, building models to analyze company projections and/or potential transactions, drafting offering memorandums for public or private financings, drafting client presentation materials, and working with clients to execute financing or merger transactions. What We're Looking For Conduct real estate industry and property-sector research, including REIT and REOC comparable company, market, and asset-level analysis. Build financial models to analyze company projections or potential transactions, including NAV, FFO/AFFO, and property-level cash flow analyses. Draft offering memorandums for public or private financings, including common stock, preferred stock, convertible and hybrid securities, and debt securities. Prepare client presentation materials for management teams and Boards of Directors. Work with clients to execute equity and debt capital markets, private placement, joint venture, and merger transactions. Some travel by car and/or in conjunction with local, regional and/or national travel, up to 10%. What You'll Bring Investment Banking Knowledge - Experience with financial modeling and analysis with significant exposure to finance and accounting; demonstrated interest in real estate, REITs, or real estate capital markets. Analytical Skills - Strong analytical and quantitative skills. Knowledge of the financial markets, the real estate industry, the analysis and reporting of financial data, and associated terminology. Time Management - Highly-motivated and energetic while managing one's time, and effectively managing multiple projects and deadlines to ensure the timely completion of all items. Personal Characteristics - Demonstrates professionalism, superior attention to detail, integrity, maturity, intellectual curiosity, initiative and good judgment; takes pride of ownership for wins and accountability for losses/mistakes with the ability to work in teams. Communication Skills - Excellent conceptualization, presentation and communication skills to effectively execute change. Education & Experience Minimum Required: Bachelor's degree in Finance, Real Estate, or related field Minimum Required: 0-2 years as a business analyst, or related experience in financial services. Recent (2026) graduates and candidates with 1-2 years of investment banking, real estate, or corporate finance experience will both be considered. Licenses & Credentials Minimum Required: None Systems & Technology Proficient in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook Preferred: Familiarity with S&P Capital IQ, FactSet, or Bloomberg, and with real estate data and valuation tools (e.g., CoStar, ARGUS) About Stifel At its core, the Stifel story is a journey of growth and optimism for the future. In our more than 125-year history, Stifel has evolved from a St. Louis-based brokerage house and is now a full-service investment bank, offering securities brokerage, trading, research, underwriting and corporate advisory services globally. Our expertise spans sectors and products in both public and private markets. We are driven by relationships, not transactions, and are committed to earning long-term trust from our clients. Our investment banking division provides a broad range of industry-leading services to its clients, including merger and acquisition advisory services, debt and equity financings, balance sheet restructuring, and mutual thrift & insurance company conversions. The combination of a full-service product offering and more than 600 bankers’ deep domain and product expertise allows us to provide solutions that meet the evolving needs of our clients. Stifel’s success is rooted in the power of our people and platform. We provide our employees an entrepreneurial environment that rewards collaboration and hard work. We are looking to engage with and hire talented candidates from all backgrounds – specifically, those who have the desire to expand their skills and realize ambitious goals. drawn.title: Relationship Manager
drawn.body:
Stratos Wealth Partners | Remote | Travel up to 50%
The Opportunity:
Stratos Wealth Partners is building a national platform for advisors who want to preserve their independence while gaining access to deeper resources, stronger technology, and broader investment capabilities. As Relationship Manager, you will be the primary point of connection for a regional portfolio of affiliated advisors and firms, helping them get the most from the platform and ensuring Stratos delivers on its commitments.
This is a role for someone who genuinely enjoys the business of advice. You will own the relationship end to end: understanding each advisor's growth ambitions, connecting them to the right capability at the right moment, clearing what gets in their way, and holding the enterprise accountable to the commitments it makes. You will work from a [hybrid base] in your region and travel up to 50 percent to be present where your advisors are.
What you will do:
Own the Relationship

• Serve as the primary relationship lead for an assigned regional portfolio of Stratos-affiliated advisors and firms, from day-to-day service coordination through long-term business planning.

• Build trusted relationships with advisors, principals, and key operating staff; learn their business models, economics, and priorities; and maintain a deliberate engagement cadence.

• Develop practical relationship plans that capture business objectives, goals, opportunities, risks, commitments, and next actions to drive organic growth and operational efficiency.

• Lead recurring business reviews that connect relationship goals to service performance, growth priorities, platform capabilities, and agreed measures of success.

• Monitor relationship health and early signals of retention risk, coordinate timely intervention, and escalate material concerns through established channels.

Drive Advisor Growth and Platform Value

• Identify and pursue growth opportunities with your firms, including organic growth, asset consolidation, referral development, practice-management support, and expanded use of Stratos capabilities.

• Help advisors understand and adopt the platform, investment, custody, technology, and planning resources that genuinely fit their business model.

• Partner with sales and subject-matter experts to qualify opportunities, coordinate discovery, and maintain clear ownership through resolution or handoff.

• Drive adoption of Stratos’ Advisor Insights Platform, Stratos Investment Management’s offerings, and SEI’s custody and investment solutions.

• Carry advisor feedback and competitive insight back into Stratos so we sharpen what we build and how we serve.

Coordinate, Resolve, and Execute

• Act as the advisor's advocate and quarterback across service, operations, product, technology, compliance, investments, practice management, onboarding, and sales.

• Clarify ownership, timelines, dependencies, and communications for client requests and initiatives.

• Lead resolution of routine and moderately complex issues, and escalate regulatory, legal, reputational, contractual, or high-impact commercial matters promptly.

• Maintain accurate relationship plans, opportunities, meeting notes, action items, risk indicators, and reporting in our CRM and reporting tools.

• Work within applicable policies, procedures, licensing requirements, supervisory expectations, and documentation standards.

How Success will be Measured:
Performance in this role is evaluated across a balanced set of relationship, growth, and execution outcomes:

• Advisor and firm retention, satisfaction, and overall relationship health as measured by Net Promoter Score and direct affiliate feedback.

• Execution of relationship plans and business-review commitments.

• Organic growth, qualified referrals, and expansion opportunities within the portfolio.

• Appropriate adoption and utilization of Stratos and SEI capabilities.

• Timely issue resolution, effective escalation, and strong cross-functional partnership.

• Quality of CRM records, forecast accuracy, documentation, and control discipline.

Compensation consists of a competitive base salary plus performance-based incentive compensation tied to these outcomes.
Why this Role Matters:
Advisors choose Stratos because they want to stay independent without going at it alone. The Relationship Manager is where that choice is proven, every single day. Do this job well and advisors grow faster, run better businesses, and stay for the long term, and the enterprise we are building gets stronger with every relationship you deepen.
Benefits and Rewards:
To help you stay energized, engaged, and inspired, we offer a wide range of benefits through our parent company, SEI, including comprehensive care for your physical and mental well-being, a strong retirement plan, tuition reimbursement, a hybrid working environment, support for working parents, and flexible time off so you can relax, recharge, and be there for the people you care about.
Equal Employment Opportunity:
Stratos Wealth Partners and SEI are equal opportunity and affirmative action employers. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

What we need from you

• At least five years of relevant experience in wealth management, registered investment advisers, advisor platforms, custody, asset management, broker-dealer services, financial technology, or a closely related client-facing financial-services environment.

• Demonstrated success managing ongoing business relationships and coordinating solutions across multiple internal teams.

• Working knowledge of advisor practice models, wealth-management operations, investment and custody concepts, platform technology, and the regulatory environment supporting RIAs and hybrid firms.

• Ability to lead a business conversation, communicate clearly, manage competing priorities, and turn complex issues into practical next steps.

• Strong analytical judgment and comfort using CRM, reporting, presentation, and collaboration tools to manage a portfolio.

• Active FINRA Series 65 or Series 66 registration.

• A bachelor's degree in business, finance, economics, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

• Willingness to travel up to 50 percent to support advisor meetings, events, and territory coverage.

What we would like from you

• Experience supporting independent advisors, RIAs, hybrid firms, affiliated practices, or multi-custody environments.

• FINRA Series 7 registration, and a CFP, CIMA, CRPC, or CFA designation.

• Fluency with CRM, portfolio accounting, financial planning, and custodial platforms.

• Experience facilitating business reviews, relationship plans, advisor events, or practice-management conversations.

• Comfort in a growing organization where process is still being built, tested, and improved.

• Someone who will embody our values of People First, Empower Entrepreneurs, Positive Can-Do Attitude, Embrace Collaboration and Do the Right Thing.

Location:

Job Summary
Be a problem solver, trusted advisor, and partner to the people and businesses in our KeyBank communities. Personal Bankers engage clients in deeper conversations to uncover needs and provide guidance and solutions to assist in client's financial wellness both in person and through proactive calling efforts. As part of the branch team, the Personal Banker will work toward attracting new clients to Key and work with existing clients to develop and expand relationships based on their unique financial goals, leading to client confidence in their finances. The Personal Banker is a client first, sales-driven, self-motivated, and competitive individual. Strong and effective teamwork, paired with communication polish and confidence, are critical for this role. At KeyBank, we believe it's our opportunity and our privilege to help our clients move forward in their financial journey. We take pride in serving our clients and making them feel that no bank will fight harder for them.

Essential Functions

• Embodies a strong client experience culture, being present with every client and teammate and realizing the impact we can have on their day, personally, professionally, and financially.
• Listen for clues for financial wellness opportunities during in-person and over the phone client conversations and provide effective and customized financial wellness recommendations to clients.
• Consistently attains individual activity, behavior, and outcome goals and expectations.
• Opening personal and business accounts (consumer checking, small business, various deposit products, home equity, unsecured lending, certificates of deposit, etc.).
• Developing strong partnerships with branch teammates and line of business partners – focusing on client acquisition and deepening the relationship of current clients; effectively managing internal and external centers of influence.
• Ensuring compliance with operational, risk, security and audit procedures and policies including appropriate documentation of client interactions.
• Support of branch operations including assisting with client transactions on the Teller line as needed.
• Participate in and occasionally facilitate in-person morning huddles and end of day debriefs.
• Work on Saturdays as directed by management.
• Performs other duties as assigned; duties, responsibilities and/or activities may change or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice
• Complies with all KeyBank policies and procedures, including without limitation, acting professionally at all times, conducting business ethically, avoiding conflicts of interest, and acting in the best interests of Key’s clients and Key.

Education

• High School Diploma , GED or equivalent business experience (required) or
• Bachelor's Degree (preferred)

Work Experience

• 1+ years Experience in developing current and new customer relationships, achieving sales goals, and building referral sources. Experience with sales is more important than financial services experience. KeyBank provides the tools and training, but we need relationship builders with a curious nature who are great at sparking conversations. (required)
• Understanding of consumer credit - including loan to value, debt to income and credit reports. (required)
• Foundational knowledge of sales and service techniques with clients, including tele-consulting, outside calling, prospecting, and networking. (required)
• Comfortable interacting with small business clients, overcoming objection, and asking fact-finding questions with the goal of being helpful. (preferred)
• Demonstrated experience with influencing business partners and leveraging centers of influence, as this role will require significant influence of partners such as Key Investment Services, Mortgage and Business Banking sales professionals. (required)
• Working knowledge of PCs (MS Windows and Office Products including Word, Excel, etc.). (required)
• Working knowledge of digital technology (mobile, apps, web-based browsing) and ability to educate clients on digital platforms and capabilities within Key (required)

Licenses and Certifications

• Notary License (preferred)

Skills

• Is knowledgeable about the client’s accounts and business with the bank and uses sound judgment with clients and transactions.
• Demonstrated ability to attain sales and referral goals through preset appointments and quality conversations leading to recommendations that support clients’ financial wellness goals, leveraging system generated lead lists, walk-ins, and professional contacts.
• Strong work ethic and high level of integrity.
• Excellent time management skills.
• Building and nurturing relationships with clients including identifying potential clients, engaging with them to understand their needs, and developing strategies to convert them into long-term clients. It also includes deepening relationships with existing clients by offering additional products and services that meet their evolving needs.
• Being attentive to client needs, resolving issues promptly, and ensuring a positive banking experience. Excellent client service helps build trust and encourages clients to continue banking with KeyBank.
• Ability to evaluate financial information to understand clients' financial health, identify investment opportunities, and recommend strategies.
• Understanding and managing risks associated with banking operations and client transactions.
• Strong verbal and non-verbal communication skills to understand clients' needs and recommend appropriate banking products and services.
• Accurate and efficient handling of cash transactions.

Core Competencies

• All KeyBank employees are expected to demonstrate Key’s Values and abide by Key’s Code of Conduct.

Physical Demands

• Consumer Retail - Prolonged Standing (5-8 hours per day), frequent use of hands to manipulate/grasp objects, ability to communicate face to face and on the phone with clients, occasional bending and lifting from floor height, frequent forward reach, frequent lifting of 1 – 10 lbs., occasional lifting of up to 30 lbs.

Driving Requirements

• Ability to routinely and frequently operate a motor vehicle with a valid driver's license.

Overview

Baker Tilly is a leading advisory, tax and assurance firm, providing clients with a genuine coast-to-coast and global advantage in major regions of the U.S. and in many of the world’s leading financial centers – New York, London, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Chicago and Boston. Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and Baker Tilly US, LLP (Baker Tilly) provide professional services through an alternative practice structure in accordance with the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct and applicable laws, regulations and professional standards. Baker Tilly US, LLP is a licensed independent CPA firm that provides attest services to its clients. Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and its subsidiary entities provide tax and business advisory services to their clients. Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and its subsidiary entities are not licensed CPA firms.
Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and Baker Tilly US, LLP, trading as Baker Tilly, are independent members of Baker Tilly International, a worldwide network of independent accounting and business advisory firms in 141 territories, with 43,000 professionals and a combined worldwide revenue of $5.2 billion. Visit bakertilly.com or join the conversation on LinkedIn, Facebook and Instagram.

Please discuss the work location status with your Baker Tilly talent acquisition professional to understand the requirements for an opportunity you are exploring.

Baker Tilly is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability or protected veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected basis, in accordance with applicable federal, state or local law.

Any unsolicited resumes submitted through our website or to Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP, employee e-mail accounts are considered property of Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP, and are not subject to payment of agency fees. In order to be an authorized recruitment agency ("search firm") for Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP, there must be a formal written agreement in place and the agency must be invited, by Baker Tilly's Talent Attraction team, to submit candidates for review via our applicant tracking system.

Job Description:

Do you have experience in the world of servicing our Public Sector and are searching for your next challenge?

Are you interested in joining one of the fastest growing public accounting firms?
If yes, consider joining Baker Tilly LLP (BT) as a Manager! Our practice recognizes the unique challenges of public entities providing consulting and internal auditing for various public sector entities, including state, local, and tribal governments as well as public utilities and K-12 schools. Our team includes a diverse array of talent including well versed Project Managers, Certified Internal Auditors, Certified Public Accountants, and specialists in other areas (human resources, work force planning, engineering, etc.).

You will work side-by-side with firm leadership and will be a valued mentor and coach to a group of talented staff. BT has the ability to provide you with amazing career experience working with some of the most entrepreneurial partners in our field.

You will enjoy this role if:

• You enjoy helping local governments and other entities meet their financial and community goals. This role specifically on the Baker Tilly Municipal Advisory team will assist communities with meeting their public finance needs, including capital planning, issuance of municipal bonds, developing incentive packages and state reporting requirements.
• You crave a leadership opportunity with a well-established public sector practice that continues to achieve tremendous growth.
• You want to be part of firm is invested in your success by providing the resources and support to continually sharpen your technical skills and build your career now, for tomorrow

What you will do:

• Assist public sector entities, mainly cities, towns, counties, redevelopment commission and economic development organizations, on their public finance needs and manage several projects simultaneously.
• Assist on management consulting projects for public sector organizations through financial management reporting, budget preparation and analysis, capital project planning, comprehensive financial planning, issuance of municipal bonds, and related client services.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

• Gathering data
• Preparing financial reports, research, and analysis
• Participating in client and working group meetings
• Presenting information to groups and clients
• Learn and grow from direct on the job coaching and mentoring along with participating in firm wide learning and development programs.
• Utilize your entrepreneurial skills to network and build strong relationships internally and externally with clients.
• Enjoy friendships, social activities and team outings that encourage a work-life balance.
• Occasional travel and mostly same-day travel within the state.
• Serve on client projects and assist in management of client relationships.
• Document and analyze processes, internal controls, and workflow to identify opportunities for improvement.
• Ensure alignment of resources – people, process, and technology – with key strategic goals and priority service areas.
• Develop tactical approaches to implement changes in strategy, service delivery, technology and/or policy.

Baker Tilly will offer you a variety of experience and the freedom to perform projects, meet clients and prospects that many firms would not at this level of experience. Your colleagues are fun, interesting, driven and have a strong desire to learn more about our business and grow our practice. You will have a defined long-term career path and your Performance Counselor will help guide you in your Baker Tilly career.

Qualifications

• A Bachelor's degree within business, finance, accounting, or public administration, MBA/MPA desirable but not a requirement.
• Five (5) plus years of progressive related consulting experience, including at least one (1) year serving as a project manager in managing similarly sized projects as described
• Knowledge of public sector operations broadly, specific knowledge or experience in a public sector setting - state or local government, public utility, and K-12 schools.
• Demonstrated management, analytical, organization, interpersonal, project management, communication skills, and highly developed Microsoft Suite skills (Word, Excel) required.
• Ability to provide exceptional client service, demonstrate commitment to continuous learning in order to stay current regarding applicable strategies, see the "big picture" as well as the details, display appropriate ethical knowledge and commitment, and exhibit a sense of urgency and commitment to quality and the timely completion of duties.

The pay range for this position is $66,000 to $182,200. This range represents a good-faith and reasonable estimate of the compensation the firm expects to pay for this position at the time of posting. Actual compensation will depend on a variety of relevant factors, including an applicant’s skills, experience, qualifications, professional certifications, work arrangements, geographic location, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range, and compensation decisions depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. Baker Tilly offers a compensation and benefits package to eligible employees.

drawn.title: Internal Audit - Credit Risk
drawn.body:
Summary
The Vice President, Internal Audit – Credit Risk is responsible for leading and executing audits, issue validations, risk assessments, and special projects covering credit risk management activities across banking and trading portfolios. The role provides independent assurance on the effectiveness of credit risk governance, risk management practices, internal controls, and regulatory compliance. The Vice President partners closely with Risk Management Audit leadership and key stakeholders to identify emerging risks, assess control effectiveness, and drive operational excellence within the audit function.

This role is hybrid and based in our New York City office.

Key Responsibilities
Audit Execution & Credit Risk Oversight

• Lead all phases of the audit lifecycle, including planning, fieldwork, reporting, issue validation, and follow-up activities for credit risk audits.

• Assess the identification, measurement, monitoring, and management of credit risk across business lines and products.

• Evaluate credit risk management practices across a broad range of products, including loans, interbank transactions, trade finance, foreign exchange transactions, futures, swaps, bonds, equities, and options.

• Support the development and execution of the annual risk assessment, audit plan, audit schedule, and continuous monitoring activities.

• Prepare and present management information and reporting related to credit risk audits and monitoring activities.

• Assist with maintaining the Off-Site Monitoring Program and monitoring emerging risks within assigned audit coverage areas.

Issue Validation & Regulatory Engagement

• Lead issue validation activities related to regulatory findings, internal audit observations, and third-party reviews.

• Review testing approaches, evaluate remediation plans, and assess the effectiveness and sustainability of corrective actions.

• Partner with Risk Management Audit leadership to identify control weaknesses, emerging risks, and opportunities for improvement.

• Support interactions with regulatory agencies, external auditors, and other third parties, as appropriate.

Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement

• Drive efficiency and consistency by adhering to Internal Audit policies, methodologies, and professional standards.

• Identify and implement opportunities to enhance audit effectiveness through process improvements, data analytics, and automation.

• Remain current on regulatory developments, industry trends, and emerging risks affecting credit risk management.

• Participate in special projects, working groups, and committee assignments as directed by audit leadership.

Collaboration & Talent Development

• Collaborate with audit teams, risk management, compliance, and control functions to ensure coordinated and effective coverage.

• Communicate audit findings, risk insights, and recommendations clearly and effectively to management and stakeholders.

• Provide coaching, guidance, and technical expertise to less experienced team members.

• Support Internal Audit's Quality Assurance initiatives and promote adherence to departmental standards and procedures.

Qualifications
Education

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, Computer Science, Management Information Systems, or a related field.

• Advanced degree and/or professional certifications such as CPA, CIA, CISA, CFE, CA, or MBA preferred.

Experience

• 5-8+ years of relevant experience in internal audit, external audit, risk management, regulatory supervision, or related financial services functions.

• Strong experience auditing and/or assessing credit risk management frameworks within a banking or capital markets environment.

• Knowledge of credit risk management practices, regulatory requirements, and first- and second-line risk management controls.

• Experience leading audits, issue validations, and special projects.

• Experience interacting with senior management, regulators, external auditors, and audit leadership.

Skills & Competencies

• Strong understanding of internal audit principles, risk management frameworks, internal controls, and regulatory expectations.

• Demonstrated knowledge of credit risk management and associated banking and capital markets products.

• Excellent analytical, organizational, project management, and problem-solving skills.

• Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to communicate effectively across all levels of the organization.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and work effectively in a fast-paced environment.

• Proven ability to mentor and guide staff while fostering a collaborative team environment.

• Experience leveraging data analytics and technology-enabled auditing techniques to improve audit efficiency and effectiveness.

The expected base salary ranges from $138,500.00 - $200,000.00. Salary offers are based on a wide range of factors including relevant skills, training, experience, education, and, where applicable, certifications and licenses obtained. Market and organizational factors are also considered. In addition to salary and a generous employee benefits package, successful candidates are eligible to receive a discretionary bonus.

At Cantor, our employees are our greatest asset. We look for individuals who are driven, intellectually engaged, team oriented and have a real desire to make an impact. The Metals & Mining investment banking team of Cantor is seeking a highly motivated, successful candidate to join as an Analyst in its Toronto office. The group advises clients on strategic and financial initiatives including mergers and acquisitions, equity and debt capital raises, restructurings, and other advisory assignments. Analysts are provided significant responsibility within the full transaction process, including conducting financial analyses, building valuation models, preparing presentation materials, execution of live transactions, conducting due diligence and assistance with new business development. Lean transaction teams provide Analysts with a strong learning platform early in their careers. Candidates must have a strong interest in investment banking, solid quantitative and analytical skills, and the ability to think broadly about strategic issues facing global Metals & Mining clients. A working knowledge of accounting, valuation, finance, and business strategy is required. Join Cantor Fitzgerald's Metals & Mining Investment Banking team in Toronto as an Analyst, supporting M&A, capital raises, and strategic advisory for global mining clients. Coordination of various processes, including capital raises and advisory transactions Prepare and analyze historical and projected financial information Perform financial analyses and create financial models Coordinate industry and company-specific due diligence related to transactions Perform industry research to support pitches and new business generation activities using tools such as Bloomberg, S&P Capital IQ, and LSEG Workspace Prepare confidential information memoranda, management presentations and marketing pitches for clients Organizing and participating in marketing and client meetings Work closely with senior bankers and deal teams on cross-border transactions, gaining exposure to global markets, investors, and strategic buyers 0-3 years of relevant work experience; prior investment banking experience is not required, however candidates with investment banking or relevant job experience is a plus Undergraduate degree with strong academic track record (minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5/4.0, or equivalent) Excel grasp of corporate finance, valuation, and financial accounting Self-motivated individuals who demonstrate initiative, drive, and leadership Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, managing multiple project deliverables simultaneously Strong written and verbal communication skills Salary- $100,000 - $110,000 + Discreitonary Bonus #LI-PM1

drawn.title: Operations Manager
drawn.body:
At Parkview Partners Capital Management , our philosophy is centered on building lasting relationships and providing personalized, fiduciary advice. We believe successful wealth management begins with understanding each client’s unique situation, values, and long-term priorities.
We are seeking an Operations/Practice Manager with 5–7 years of progressive experience in the wealth management industry. This individual brings demonstrated leadership capability, advanced client service expertise, and a proven ability to onboard and manage complex client relationships while driving operational excellence. This role expands beyond execution into leadership, oversight, and continuous improvement of client service operations while directly supporting financial advisors and high-net-worth clients.

WHY CHOOSE PARKVIEW PARTNERS CAPITAL MANAGEMENT?
Competitive Salary and Benefits - We offer a top-tier compensation package, including:

• Competitive Base Salary : Benchmarked against the industry’s top quartile.

• Performance Bonuses : Transparent, merit-based bonus program. We incentivize exceptional client service and interaction.

• Benefits : 100% paid medical, dental and vision insurance for employees, a 3% 401(k) match, and paid time off.

• Work Location: Our offices are in the highly desirable German Village area and have employee parking .

• Employee Engagement : We conduct annual- employee reviews, with bonuses, but are a closely held business with an open-door policy.

• Growth Opportunities: We provide every team member with a path for growth and development.

WHAT WILL YOU DO AS AN OPERATIONS/PRACTICE MANAGER?

• Operational Management : Oversee the day-to-day operations of the firm, ensuring that the office runs smoothly and efficiently. Manage scheduling, office workflows, and administrative processes.

• Team Leadership & Development : Lead and mentor the support staff. Provide guidance, training, and support to ensure that team members are productive and aligned with the firm's goals and culture.

• Client Onboarding & Relationship Management : Collaborate closely with financial advisors to ensure exceptional client service. Manage client onboarding, communications, and ensure that client needs are being met in a timely manner.

• Compliance & Risk Management : Ensure the firm is in compliance with industry regulations, company policies, and legal requirements. Work closely with compliance teams to monitor and update procedures.

• Leverage Technology to Drive Scale & Efficiencies : Ensure consistent adoption of existing technology, while seeking opportunities to identify and adopt other industry leading technologies that can drive incremental scale and efficiencies in the business and optimize the client experience.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS & CHARACTERISTICS

• Bachelor’s degree

• 5-7 years of progressive experience in practice management or operations management, ideally in a financial advisory firm.

• Additional certifications in financial services are not required, however a plus

• Strong leadership and team management abilities

• Knowledge of financial advisory practices, compliance requirements, and industry standards.

• Experience working with custodial platforms (Schwab, Fidelity, LPL, etc.)

• Proficiency in office software (Microsoft Office Suite, CRM systems, Portfolio Management software (Orion, Black Diamond, etc.).

• High degree of accuracy, attention to detail, and strong problem-solving skills

• Self-motivated, positive attitude with a collaborative mindset

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

• Base Salary : $75,000-$85,000/year

• Bonuses : Transparent, merit-based bonus program. We incentivize exceptional client service and interaction.

• Insurance : 100% paid medical, dental and vision insurance for employees.

• Retirement Savings : 3% 401(k) Match

Ready to join a team that values your contributions and invests in your growth? Apply today and become part of Parkview Partners Capital Management!

drawn.title: Quantitative Associate - Special District Group
drawn.body:
Job Description:

At Piper Sandler, we connect capital with opportunity to build a better future.

We enable growth and success of our clients through deep sector expertise, candid advice and a differentiated, highly productive culture. Our mission is to recruit, develop, and retain high-performing people that are bright, committed, and who work in partnership with others to achieve at a high level.

We are currently looking for a Quantitative Associate to join our Special District Group in our Denver, CO office. This is a full-time and in-person role. Candidates must be based in or willing to relocate to the Denver area. A working knowledge of Colorado geography and market dynamics is a plus.

About The Special District Group
The Special District Group (SDG) is a team in Piper Sandler's Public Finance practice that is dedicated to raising capital for public infrastructure for new development or redevelopment projects. We hold a dominant position in the Colorado, Utah, and Texas markets and are actively growing into new markets nationwide.

Our team leaders were amongst the pioneers of Special District financing and have been integral leaders in the sector for over 45 years. The SDG team is passionate about the quality of banking we bring to the market and the experience we offer our clients and partners. We are unwavering in our belief that our team’s shared success precedes the pursuit of individual aspirations. We have a deep commitment to high-touch communication and collaborative relationships, and we believe that our team’s expertise, creativity, and resilience are critical to our success.

About This Critical Role
We are seeking a Quantitative Associate to join the SDG team in Denver, Colorado. The SDG Quantitative Team provides the analytical foundation for our practice, developing the financial models and debt structures necessary to fund large-scale infrastructure and real estate development. As a Quantitative Associate, you will work at the intersection of investment banking and financial analysis, delivering the data-driven insights required to structure complex transactions.

About The Ideal Candidate
The ideal candidate is passionate about financial modeling, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and possesses the ability to navigate multiple priorities with strong organizational skills. You must display the professional maturity required to interact effectively with senior partners, clients, and colleagues.

• Financial Structuring: Develop, refine, and stress-test sophisticated financial models that serve as the foundation for real estate-based public finance transactions.
• Analytical Rigor : Provide high-level numerical analysis and debt service modeling, ensuring accuracy and strategic alignment from deal inception through final execution.
• Process Innovation : Conceptualize and implement new modeling methodologies and technical solutions to improve operational efficiency and analytical precision. You are encouraged to challenge existing processes and propose improvements to our quantitative toolkit.
• Strategic Collaboration : Partner directly with senior bankers to translate complex client objectives into viable financial structures. Your analysis will serve as a primary driver in the decision-making process.
• Transaction Management : Navigate multiple, overlapping transaction timelines with precision, ensuring that all quantitative deliverables meet the high standards of our practice.
• Technical Leadership : Contribute to the ongoing evolution of our quantitative systems, including the integration of advanced Excel automation and internal AI tools.
• Team Development : Collaborate with the Quantitative Team to share technical expertise, mentor junior members, and foster a culture of continuous improvement and high performance.
• Organizational Stewardship : Consistently model SDG’s values and contribute to the professional development and collaborative culture of the team.

Technical & Professional Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree preferred. Security Industry Essentials (SIE) certification is a plus.
• 2+ years of relevant experience in real estate investment, underwriting, investment banking, or municipal bond analysis.
• Advanced proficiency in cash flow modeling and Excel. You view modeling as an exercise in precision and efficiency, not just data entry.
• Proficiency in MS Office and database management. A demonstrated interest in leveraging AI tools and automation to enhance modeling workflows is highly valued. Experience with DBC Finance is a plus.
• A proven ability to distill complex financial variables into clear, actionable insights for diverse stakeholders.

Core Competencies:

• Self-reflective, proactive in identifying growth opportunities, and committed to setting ambitious professional goals.
• Questions conventional approaches and proposes original, resourceful ideas.
• Exhibits conviction when presenting ideas and chooses courage over comfort when facing difficult tasks.
• Works cooperatively with diverse styles and builds strong partnerships inside and outside the organization.
• Manages workflow by establishing clear tasks, meeting deadlines, and maintaining proactive communication.

Piper Sandler is a leading investment bank, enabling growth and success for our clients through deep sector expertise, candid advice, and a differentiated, highly productive culture. With more than 1,700 employees across 60 offices world-wide, we offer our clients the scale needed to meet their capital needs with local support from experts in the field. Learn more about the firm here .

Piper Sandler values a strong culture dedicated to the emotional and physical well-being of our employees. Learn more about our commitment to our employee’s health, well-being, our benefits program and how we are here for our employees and their families today, tomorrow and beyond here .

The anticipated base salary for this position is $100,000 per year. This position is eligible for substantial, additional incentive compensation in the first year and beyond. We are committed to hiring the right talent; for candidates with significant, directly relevant experience, we are open to discussing a higher title and compensation package commensurate with their background.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, marital status, status as a protected veteran or status with regard to public assistance.

Line of Business:

The Premier Banker is an experienced banker, servicing as the primary contact for a complex client portfolio of mass affluent clients. Through proactive outreach, this role manages mass affluent clients' complete banking relationship and connects clients to specialists to ensure all financial needs are met. The objective of the role is to grow, deepen, and retain client relationships by delivering TD’s model of convenience, sales, and advice, and differentiating with a personalized, connected experience. Depth & Scope:

• Consultative sales experience required

Customer Accountabilities:

• Requires established client service skills to perform a broad range of both routine and multi-step Customer transactions
• Establishes and nurtures client relationships through proactive outreach, ongoing engagement, consistent display of product knowledge, actively listening to client needs and offering advice based solutions or partner referrals.

• Delivers client end-to-end advice they expect: (1) building trust with educational content & tools, (2) providing consultative support, and (3) advocating for them with proactive insights & recommendations

• Ensures documentation that is prepared / completed is accurate and properly reflects client/ business intentions and is consistent with relevant rules / regulations
• Applies Compliance policies and regulations to all transactions to ensure integrity of proper compliance with all documentation that operational requirements are followed and that the appropriate documentation is recorded
• Engages in conversations with clients regarding loan applications, prepares documents, and conducts loan closings
• Meets individual / Store performance metrics

• Is an active participant in personal performance and development activities
• Acts as a brand champion both internally and externally
• Collaborates with team members in contributing to the success of the team and organization
• Partners as a team player

• Detail oriented, well organized, self-starter with high energy level
• Actively seeks opportunities to improve delivery of work with high attention to quality standards

• Is engaged in advancing and sustaining a unique, inclusive culture that reflects TD's diversity agenda, and creates an extraordinary employee experience
